title: Task 2: Exact lookup_srd store and tool facade
description: Objective: Implement exact lookup by ref or canonical name and kind over the bundled SRD catalog. Files: modify packages/core/src/srd/store.ts; create packages/core/src/srd/lookup.ts; modify packages/core/test/srd.test.ts. Steps: 1. Add failing tests for lookupSrd({ kind: monster, ref: monster:goblin }), lookupSrd({ kind: spell, name: Fire Bolt }), and lookupSrd({ kind: class, name: Fighter }). Add failing tests that Gob and wrong-kind Fire Bolt as monster return a typed not_found result. Command: npm run test -- packages/core/test/srd.test.ts. Expected RED: lookupSrd is not exported. 2. Implement exact indexes by kind/ref and normalized full name only; do not add fuzzy or substring matching. 3. Run focused test to GREEN. 4. Run npm run build and npm run test. 5. Commit the task changes.
design: store.ts owns buildSrdIndex(catalog) and lookupSrdRecord(input, catalog = SRD_CATALOG). lookup.ts exports lookupSrd(input): SrdLookupResult as the tool-facing API. Result shape is { ok: true, record, license } or { ok: false, code: 'not_found', message }. Name normalization trims and collapses whitespace and lowercases; it must still require complete exact names.
acceptance_criteria: Known monster, spell, and class build option resolve by ref or exact name; fuzzy/partial and wrong-kind lookups fail deterministically; full test suite passes.
close_reason: Added exact SRD lookup by kind-scoped ref or complete normalized name, with typed not_found failures for partial, unknown, and wrong-kind inputs; verification: npm run build passed and npm run test passed with 24 passed / 1 skipped; TDD evidence recorded.

comments.author: Joseph Bongaarts
comments.text: RED verification: npm run test -- packages/core/test/srd.test.ts -> failed for expected reason: ../src/srd/lookup.js does not exist.

comments.author: Joseph Bongaarts
comments.text: Debugging evidence: npm run build failed at packages/core/src/srd/store.ts with TS2345, input.name is string | undefined. Root cause: the union used optional never fields, so the 'ref' in input check does not narrow the name branch enough for strict TypeScript. Fix: narrow on input.ref !== undefined so the else branch has a defined name.

Debugging verification: TS2345 narrowing issue fixed and build rerun passed.
